name: California
permitAge: 15 and a half (under 18), with driver education completed; permit valid for driving once behind-the-wheel training starts (handbook p. 3)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours with a California-licensed driver 25 or older, 10 of them at night (handbook p. 3)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months, or until age 18, before the drive test (handbook p. 3)
teen.nightLimit: First 12 months of provisional license: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. (handbook p. 4) unless with a licensed parent/guardian, a licensed driver 25 or older, or a certified instructor (CHP); exceptions with notes for medical need, school, work, family (handbook p. 4)
teen.passengerLimit: No passengers under 20 unless a parent/guardian or a California-licensed driver 25 or older rides along (handbook p. 4); first 12 months (CHP)
teen.phone: Under 18: no cell phone or wireless device to call or text while driving, except an emergency call (handbook p. 71; VC 23124 includes hands-free). Adults: hands-free only (handbook p. 70).

bac.under21: 0.01 (handbook p. 73); 0.05 or more can lead to a DUI arrest (p. 75); DUI conviction at 0.01 for under 21: revocation for one year (p. 75)

notes: Handbook checked: California Driver's Handbook DL 600 English, REV. 6/2025 (PDF dated June/August 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Page numbers are the printed page numbers.

Knowledge test: multiple choice, three attempts per application, minors wait 7 days after a failure (handbook p. 5). The handbook does not give the number of questions or the pass mark; third-party sites say 46 under 18 and 36 for adults with 80 percent. Not confirmed on dmv.ca.gov, so left null.

Test languages not stated in the handbook. The handbook is published in 10 languages; the online DL application is in 10 languages (English, Spanish, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Khmer, Korean, Tagalog, Thai, Vietnamese) per dmv.ca.gov, but that is the application, not the test.
Minors wait 14 days after a failed drive test (handbook p. 6).

Speed: 65 mph most highways unless posted, 55 two-lane undivided and towing (p. 67); 25 residential/business (p. 52); 15 alleys, blind intersections, near unseen railroad crossings (p. 51); 25 near schools (p. 50). The handbook does not mention 70 mph freeways.
Right on red after full stop unless NO TURN ON RED (p. 18); left on red only one-way to one-way (p. 20).
School bus: no need to stop on the other side of a divided or multilane highway with two or more lanes each way (p. 51).

Move over: the 2025 handbook (p. 49) covers emergency vehicles, tow trucks and road work vehicles only. AB 390 (effective 2026-01-01) reportedly extends it to any stationary vehicle with hazard lights; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov was not reachable (bot check), so ca-029 stays medium.
Curb colors (p. 28); 15 ft from fire hydrant (p. 28). Headlights when wipers needed for fog, rain, snow (p. 11).
Lane splitting by motorcycles is legal and defined (AB 51, 2016); not used in questions.
